title: Elekta Versa HD Radiation Therapy System - Calibration or Quality-Control Test Fails
description: A calibration or quality-control check does not complete or meet expectations because of setup, positioning, test equipment, environment, readiness, or system conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patients and Suspend Affected Clinical Use
steps.instructions: If a required QC or calibration check has failed, do not use the affected function clinically unless departmental policy specifically permits continued use. Expected outcome: The failed verification does not create an unrecognized patient-treatment risk.

steps.title: 2. Identify the Exact Failed Test
steps.instructions: Record the name of the calibration or QC procedure, the point at which it failed, the displayed message, and whether failure occurred during setup, acquisition, analysis, or completion. Expected outcome: The exact failed process is identified rather than treating all QC failures as equivalent.

steps.title: 3. Verify Test Setup
steps.instructions: Confirm that the correct test device, phantom, accessory, fixture, positioning arrangement, and workflow are being used according to approved procedures. Expected outcome: The test setup matches the approved method.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Test Equipment
steps.instructions: Check accessible test equipment for damage, contamination, depleted batteries where applicable, loose cables, incorrect connection, or expired calibration status. Do not use test equipment with questionable accuracy. Expected outcome: The independent test equipment is suitable for use.

steps.title: 5. Verify System Readiness and Positioning
steps.instructions: Confirm that the Versa HD and relevant imaging, positioning, or treatment subsystems have completed startup and are in the required state for the test. Verify gantry, table, detector, and accessory positions as applicable. Expected outcome: The system is correctly configured externally for the intended test.

steps.title: 6. Check Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Check for unusual temperature, power, HVAC, construction, vibration, or other room conditions that could affect a sensitive QC measurement. Expected outcome: No obvious environmental condition is compromising the test.

steps.title: 7. Repeat the Approved Test Once
steps.instructions: After correcting any setup issue, repeat the approved QC or calibration check according to the established procedure. Do not repeatedly rerun a failing calibration in an attempt to force a pass. Expected outcome: The test completes normally and meets the department's approved acceptance criteria.

steps.title: 8. Compare With Previous Results
steps.instructions: If available, compare the current result with prior documented QC or calibration results to determine whether the change is abrupt, gradual, or isolated. Expected outcome: The result provides useful evidence about whether the problem is a setup anomaly or a persistent system change.

steps.title: 9. Verify Any Corrected Function
steps.instructions: If the failure is traced to an external setup or test-equipment issue, repeat the applicable verification using the corrected setup before clinical use. Expected outcome: The system successfully passes the required verification. Troubleshooting can stop after documentation and return-to-service requirements are completed.

steps.title: 10. Escalate a Repeated Failure
steps.instructions: If the approved test continues to fail after external setup, test equipment, positioning, readiness, and environmental causes have been ruled out, stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The affected system or function remains out of clinical service pending qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Radiation Oncology reported that a scheduled Versa HD imaging QC test repeatedly failed.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the QC phantom was incorrectly positioned for the approved test procedure.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering corrected the phantom setup, repeated the approved QC test successfully, and documented the passing result before return to service.

title: Elekta Versa HD Radiation Therapy System - Cooling, Fan, or Overtemperature Fault Occurs
description: The system reports cooling, fan, or temperature problems caused by blocked airflow, room conditions, facility cooling, external contamination, or service-level cooling faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Stop Treatment if Required
steps.instructions: If the system reports an overtemperature or cooling fault that affects safe operation, discontinue treatment according to departmental procedures. Do not continue operating overheating equipment merely because treatment can still be initiated. Expected outcome: The patient is safe and the equipment is not operated under an unresolved thermal fault.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Thermal Complaint
steps.instructions: Record the exact displayed message and determine whether the fault appears at startup, during idle operation, during imaging, or during treatment activity. Check for unusual fan noise, odor, heat, or repeated shutdown. Expected outcome: The thermal condition and its operating context are clearly documented.

steps.title: 3. Check Room Temperature and HVAC
steps.instructions: Determine whether the treatment room and equipment spaces appear normally conditioned and whether building HVAC is functioning. Check for recent HVAC alarms, maintenance, or room temperature changes. Expected outcome: The equipment is operating in a normally conditioned environment or a facility HVAC problem is identified.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Accessible Airflow Paths
steps.instructions: Check accessible ventilation openings, external filters intended for routine inspection, and surrounding clearances for dust buildup, blocked airflow, stored items, or coverings. Do not open internal enclosures for fan servicing unless authorized. Expected outcome: External airflow paths are clear.

steps.title: 5. Listen for Accessible Fan Operation
steps.instructions: From outside the equipment, note whether expected cooling fans appear to be operating and whether there is abnormal grinding, rattling, surging, or absence of airflow. Expected outcome: External observations do not indicate an obvious cooling failure. Any abnormal fan behavior supports removal from service and escalation.

steps.title: 6. Check for External Heat Sources
steps.instructions: Verify that portable heaters, temporary equipment, blocked returns, direct sunlight, relocated cabinets, or other external changes are not increasing equipment temperature. Expected outcome: No external heat source is contributing to the condition.

steps.title: 7. Allow Approved Cool-Down if Appropriate
steps.instructions: If permitted by site and manufacturer procedures, allow the equipment to cool while powered down or placed in the appropriate safe state. Do not repeatedly restart equipment that immediately returns to an overtemperature condition. Expected outcome: A transient environmental condition clears without recurrence.

steps.title: 8. Verify Operation After Correction
steps.instructions: If an external airflow or environmental cause was corrected, restart using the approved procedure and monitor the system through an appropriate nonclinical functional check. Expected outcome: No cooling or overtemperature fault returns and system operation remains stable.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Recurring or Unexplained Thermal Faults
steps.instructions: If the fault returns, a fan sounds abnormal, equipment remains unusually hot, or no external cause is identified, stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The Versa HD remains out of service until the thermal problem is evaluated by qualified service personnel.

CCR.Complaint: Radiation Oncology reported that the Versa HD displayed a cooling fault and would not remain treatment ready.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an accessible ventilation path obstructed by equipment stored against the system enclosure.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering removed the obstruction, allowed the system to cool, completed an approved restart, and verified stable operation without recurrence before return to service.

title: Elekta Versa HD Radiation Therapy System - Detector or Acquisition Hardware Is Not Ready
description: Imaging detector or acquisition hardware does not reach ready status because of positioning, connections, startup state, accessories, power, or communication conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Suspend Imaging or Treatment
steps.instructions: Do not proceed with treatment or image-guided positioning when required acquisition hardware is unavailable or unreliable. Move the patient to a safe condition according to departmental procedures if continued positioning depends on imaging. Expected outcome: No treatment or positioning decision depends on unavailable acquisition hardware.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Affected Hardware
steps.instructions: Identify which detector, imaging panel, acquisition component, or workstation is reported as not ready. Record the exact status message and determine whether the condition occurs continuously or only during a specific workflow. Expected outcome: The affected acquisition path is clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify System Startup and Readiness
steps.instructions: Confirm that the relevant imaging hardware and associated workstation have completed normal startup and are not still initializing. Check for other subsystems that also failed to become ready. Expected outcome: All required external components are powered and the problem is isolated to the acquisition function.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Detector Position and External Obstructions
steps.instructions: Verify that movable detector hardware is positioned as required for the intended imaging operation and that nothing is obstructing deployment or alignment. Do not force detector movement. Expected outcome: Detector hardware is correctly positioned without external interference.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Accessible Connections
steps.instructions: Check accessible power, data, network, synchronization, and control cables associated with the imaging hardware for looseness, damage, strain, or disconnection. Reseat only connections intended for normal external service access. Expected outcome: External acquisition connections are secure and undamaged.

steps.title: 6. Check Accessories and Imaging Setup
steps.instructions: Confirm that required accessories and imaging-related components are installed correctly and that no unrelated accessory or positioning configuration is preventing readiness. Expected outcome: The imaging setup matches the intended workflow and no external accessory condition is blocking acquisition.

steps.title: 7. Check Workstation and Communication Status
steps.instructions: Verify that the imaging workstation is responsive and that applicable communication links between the workstation and treatment system appear available. If the workstation is frozen or disconnected, address that external condition before assuming detector failure. Expected outcome: The acquisition workstation communicates normally with the system.

steps.title: 8. Perform an Approved Reinitialization
steps.instructions: If site procedures permit and no patient is dependent on the system, perform an approved restart or reinitialization of the affected external acquisition workflow. Avoid repeated restarts if the same fault immediately returns. Expected outcome: The acquisition hardware reaches its normal ready state.

steps.title: 9. Verify Imaging Function
steps.instructions: Using approved quality-control or nonclinical verification methods, confirm that the detector initializes, acquires an image, and communicates normally. Do not return the system to treatment use solely because a ready indicator appears. Expected outcome: The acquisition path functions normally and consistently. Troubleshooting can stop after applicable imaging verification is completed.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Readiness Problems
steps.instructions: If the hardware does not reach ready status after external position, power, connection, workstation, and initialization checks, stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The affected system remains out of service pending qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Radiation Oncology reported that the Elekta Versa HD imaging detector remained not ready and image acquisition could not begin.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a loose external data connection at the acquisition hardware interface.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the connection, reinitialized the imaging workflow, verified successful image acquisition, and confirmed normal readiness before return to service.

title: Elekta Versa HD Radiation Therapy System - DICOM, PACS, or Worklist Transfer Fails
description: Patient, image, or worklist data does not transfer correctly because of network connectivity, destination availability, identifiers, interface configuration, or infrastructure problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Clinical Workflow
steps.instructions: Do not proceed with treatment using uncertain patient identification, incomplete transferred data, or an unverified workaround. Follow departmental procedures for any downtime workflow. Expected outcome: Patient identification and treatment data integrity remain protected during troubleshooting.

steps.title: 2. Define the Failed Transaction
steps.instructions: Determine whether the failure involves DICOM image transfer, PACS communication, modality worklist retrieval, patient data exchange, or another network transaction. Record the source, intended destination, and exact failure behavior. Expected outcome: The specific data path being tested is clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify Local Network Connectivity
steps.instructions: Check the Versa HD workstation or applicable interface for normal network connection and visible link indications. Inspect accessible network cables and patch connections for damage or disconnection. Expected outcome: The local network connection is physically intact.

steps.title: 4. Determine Whether Other Network Functions Work
steps.instructions: Check whether the affected workstation can communicate with other normally available systems or whether multiple network functions are unavailable. Expected outcome: The problem is localized to one destination or identified as a broader network outage.

steps.title: 5. Verify Destination Availability
steps.instructions: Determine whether PACS, worklist, oncology information, or other destination systems are operational and accessible to other clinical devices. Coordinate with IT or the responsible application team when necessary. Expected outcome: The receiving system is confirmed available or an external infrastructure outage is identified.

steps.title: 6. Verify Patient and Study Information
steps.instructions: Check that the intended patient, study, and workflow information is selected correctly and that the failure is not caused by an obvious mismatch or incomplete entry. Do not modify clinical identifiers simply to force a transfer. Expected outcome: The transaction is being attempted with the intended patient and study information.

steps.title: 7. Review Visible Communication Configuration
steps.instructions: Verify only authorized, visible configuration information such as intended destination selection or normal user-accessible network targets. Do not alter protected network, DICOM, or service configuration without authorization. Expected outcome: The expected destination is selected and no obvious user-level configuration error is present.

steps.title: 8. Retry a Controlled Transfer
steps.instructions: After correcting any external connectivity or destination issue, retry an appropriate nonclinical or authorized transaction. Expected outcome: The data transfers successfully to the intended system.

steps.title: 9. Confirm End-to-End Receipt
steps.instructions: Verify at the receiving system that the correct data arrived completely and is associated with the intended patient or test record. Expected outcome: End-to-end communication is confirmed. Troubleshooting can stop once transfer and data integrity are verified.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Interface Failure
steps.instructions: If the transfer still fails after physical network, destination availability, patient information, and approved configuration checks, stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The issue is escalated to the appropriate Elekta, IT, PACS, oncology information system, or network support resource.

CCR.Complaint: Radiation Oncology reported that Versa HD imaging studies would not transfer to the configured destination.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external network cable at the affected workstation was disconnected.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering restored the network connection, repeated the transfer, and verified successful receipt of the correct study at the destination system.

helpfulDetails: Whether other devices can reach the destination

title: Elekta Versa HD Radiation Therapy System - Exposure or Scan Will Not Start or Is Aborted
description: Imaging exposure or scan will not begin or terminates unexpectedly because of interlocks, readiness, positioning, workflow, control, or communication conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Stop Repeated Attempts
steps.instructions: Do not repeatedly attempt imaging or treatment-related exposures while the cause of an abort is unknown. Maintain patient safety and follow departmental procedures if a patient must be removed from the treatment position. Expected outcome: No unnecessary exposure or unsafe treatment delay occurs during troubleshooting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the exposure never begins, starts and immediately aborts, or stops partway through acquisition. Record the exact on-screen message and the workflow step at which the failure occurs. Expected outcome: The failure is reproducible and clearly associated with a specific stage of acquisition.

steps.title: 3. Verify System Readiness
steps.instructions: Confirm that required treatment and imaging subsystems show their normal ready status before initiation. Check whether detectors, positioning components, workstations, and acquisition hardware are fully initialized. Expected outcome: All required components are ready before the exposure command is issued.

steps.title: 4. Check Safety and Room Conditions
steps.instructions: Verify that accessible emergency controls, door-related status indications, and other external safety conditions appear normal. Do not bypass any treatment-room or equipment safety interlock. Expected outcome: No external safety condition is intentionally preventing the exposure or scan.

steps.title: 5. Verify Positioning and Equipment Deployment
steps.instructions: Confirm that the gantry, table, detector, and other required equipment are positioned appropriately for the intended imaging workflow and that no obstruction exists. Expected outcome: The physical setup permits the requested acquisition.

steps.title: 6. Verify Controls and Selected Workflow
steps.instructions: Confirm that the correct patient, study, imaging workflow, and acquisition selection are active and that no obvious incomplete workflow step is preventing initiation. Do not change clinical parameters merely to force an exposure to occur. Expected outcome: The intended workflow is correctly selected and logically ready to proceed.

steps.title: 7. Inspect External Acquisition Connections
steps.instructions: Check accessible connections between imaging hardware, workstations, controls, and network interfaces. Look for loose cables, damaged connectors, or peripherals that have lost power. Expected outcome: External acquisition and control connections are intact.

steps.title: 8. Repeat Using an Approved Nonclinical Test
steps.instructions: After correcting any external issue, use an approved quality-control or service verification method rather than a patient exposure to determine whether acquisition now starts and completes normally. Expected outcome: The exposure or scan initiates and completes without aborting.

steps.title: 9. Verify Complete Imaging Operation
steps.instructions: Confirm that the image is acquired, transferred to the appropriate workstation, displayed correctly, and retained as expected. Expected outcome: The complete acquisition path functions normally. Troubleshooting can stop after applicable verification requirements are met.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Exposure Failure
steps.instructions: If exposures remain inhibited or continue to abort after external readiness, controls, positioning, workflow, and communication checks, stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The system is removed from affected clinical use pending qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Radiation Oncology reported that imaging acquisitions on the Elekta Versa HD would begin but repeatedly abort before completion.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the imaging detector was not fully in its required operating position.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering corrected the detector positioning condition, completed a nonclinical acquisition successfully, and verified normal imaging operation before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether acquisition never started or aborted

title: Elekta Versa HD Radiation Therapy System - Gantry, Table, or Positioning Motion Is Unavailable
description: Gantry, treatment table, or other positioning motion is unavailable because of interlocks, controls, obstructions, positioning conditions, or external communication problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient From Unintended Motion
steps.instructions: Stop treatment activity and ensure the patient is safely supported. Do not troubleshoot unreliable positioning equipment while a patient depends on it. If necessary, follow departmental procedures for safe patient removal before technical troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The patient is safe and no unexpected equipment movement can occur during troubleshooting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Motion Is Unavailable
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem affects the gantry, treatment table, a specific axis, multiple axes, or all positioning motion. Note whether the motion command is ignored, starts and stops, is inhibited, or produces a displayed message. Expected outcome: The affected motion and exact failure behavior are clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect for Physical Obstructions
steps.instructions: Check the treatment area for accessories, immobilization devices, cables, patient-support equipment, room items, or other objects that could interfere with movement. Do not force movement past resistance. Expected outcome: The intended travel path is clear and no external obstruction is preventing motion.

steps.title: 4. Check Emergency and Safety Controls
steps.instructions: Verify that accessible emergency-stop controls and other operator safety controls are in their intended state. Do not bypass collision protection, interlocks, or safety systems. Expected outcome: Motion is not being inhibited by an externally activated safety control.

steps.title: 5. Verify Positioning Controls
steps.instructions: Inspect the applicable hand controls, pendant, console controls, or other normal positioning interfaces for damage, stuck controls, loose connections, or abnormal indicators. If an approved equivalent control method is available, compare operation using that method. Expected outcome: A functional control produces the expected positioning command. If one external control is defective while another works normally, isolate the defective control from use.

steps.title: 6. Verify Required System State
steps.instructions: Confirm that the Versa HD is in the appropriate operational state for the requested motion and that no visible interlock, mode restriction, or workflow condition is preventing movement. Do not alter protected configuration or service settings. Expected outcome: The system is in a state where the requested movement should normally be permitted.

steps.title: 7. Check Accessories and Table Attachments
steps.instructions: Inspect attached treatment accessories, indexing hardware, patient supports, immobilization devices, and external cabling for improper installation or interference. Remove or reposition only items that can safely be addressed without affecting patient setup or calibration. Expected outcome: No accessory or external attachment is mechanically or logically inhibiting movement.

steps.title: 8. Compare Motion Functions
steps.instructions: With the system out of clinical use, test other normal positioning functions to determine whether the problem is isolated or system-wide. Observe for abnormal sound, vibration, hesitation, or inconsistent movement. Expected outcome: Normal motion is smooth and repeatable. Any abnormal motion requires removal from service even if movement remains possible.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: If normal motion is restored after correcting an external condition, verify the affected movement through its normal operational range appropriate for routine service testing and confirm that controls stop motion normally. Expected outcome: The positioning function operates consistently without abnormal indications. Troubleshooting can stop after required return-to-service checks are completed.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Motion Failure
steps.instructions: If motion remains unavailable or unreliable after external controls, obstructions, accessories, interlocks, and operating state are checked, stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The system is removed from service for qualified evaluation rather than operated with unreliable positioning.

CCR.Complaint: Radiation Oncology reported that treatment table motion on the Elekta Versa HD was unavailable during patient setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an external positioning control connection was not fully seated.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the connection, verified repeatable table motion and normal stopping behavior, and completed functional checks before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether all or only one control location failed

title: Elekta Versa HD Radiation Therapy System - Image Quality Is Poor or Artifacts Are Present
description: Acquired images are degraded, inconsistent, or contain artifacts caused by positioning, accessories, contamination, setup, calibration state, or acquisition-path problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Clinical Decision-Making
steps.instructions: Do not use images of questionable quality for patient positioning, verification, or treatment decisions. If clinically necessary, use an alternate verified method according to departmental procedures. Expected outcome: No patient treatment decision relies on an image known to be unreliable.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Image-Quality Complaint
steps.instructions: Review the affected image and determine whether the issue is noise, banding, streaking, distortion, missing areas, repeated patterns, poor contrast, or another visible abnormality. Determine whether the issue affects every image or only certain workflows. Expected outcome: The artifact is clearly characterized and its reproducibility is understood.

steps.title: 3. Check Patient and Accessory Positioning
steps.instructions: Confirm that patient supports, immobilization devices, treatment accessories, cables, clothing items, or other objects are not unexpectedly within the imaging field. Expected outcome: No avoidable external object or setup condition is causing the artifact.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Accessible Detector Surfaces and Components
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible detector covers and imaging surfaces for contamination, damage, foreign material, or obvious obstruction. Clean only according to approved procedures. Expected outcome: Accessible imaging surfaces are clean and physically intact.

steps.title: 5. Verify Detector and Equipment Position
steps.instructions: Confirm that imaging hardware is fully deployed or positioned as required and that no obvious misalignment or mechanical interference is present. Expected outcome: Imaging components are correctly positioned for acquisition.

steps.title: 6. Verify Acquisition Setup
steps.instructions: Confirm that the intended imaging workflow and appropriate clinical acquisition selection are being used. Compare the issue with another appropriate approved acquisition setup when possible, without changing parameters merely to mask the problem. Expected outcome: Poor image quality is not the result of an incorrect workflow or unintended selection.

steps.title: 7. Compare With an Approved Test Object or QC Image
steps.instructions: Acquire an approved quality-control image or use an appropriate test object to determine whether the artifact persists without the patient. Expected outcome: If the artifact disappears, investigate patient setup or external objects. If it remains, the issue is likely within the imaging path or system environment.

steps.title: 8. Check Environment and External Interference
steps.instructions: Look for recent equipment changes, nearby electronic devices, cable routing changes, construction, power events, or other environmental changes that coincide with the complaint. Expected outcome: No external environmental change explains the image degradation.

steps.title: 9. Verify Image Display Path
steps.instructions: Compare the image on an appropriate local display or workstation when available to distinguish acquisition artifacts from display or transfer issues. Expected outcome: The artifact can be localized to acquisition or display/communication rather than assumed to originate from the detector.

steps.title: 10. Perform Final Image Verification
steps.instructions: After correction of an external cause, repeat an approved QC image and confirm normal image appearance and consistency. Expected outcome: The image meets the department's approved acceptance criteria. Troubleshooting can stop after required verification is complete.

steps.title: 11. Escalate Persistent Image-Quality Problems
steps.instructions: If artifacts remain after setup, accessories, detector condition, positioning, workflow, environment, and display path are checked, stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The imaging function is withheld from clinical use until qualified evaluation is completed.

CCR.Complaint: Radiation Oncology reported a repeatable artifact on Versa HD verification images that affected image interpretation.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an external positioning accessory unintentionally within the imaging field.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering repositioned the accessory, repeated the approved QC acquisition, and verified that the artifact was no longer present before return to service.

title: Elekta Versa HD Radiation Therapy System - Study Will Not Save, Reconstruct, or Export
description: An imaging study cannot save, reconstruct, or export because of workflow, storage, workstation, network, destination, or communication problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Data and Treatment Workflow
steps.instructions: Do not delete studies, repeat patient imaging, or create replacement records until the existing data and clinical impact are understood. If imaging is required for treatment decisions, follow the department's approved downtime or alternative workflow. Expected outcome: Existing patient data is protected and unnecessary repeat imaging is avoided.

steps.title: 2. Identify the Failed Operation
steps.instructions: Determine whether the study fails to save locally, fails during reconstruction, cannot be opened after reconstruction, or fails only during export. Record the exact message and the point where processing stops. Expected outcome: The problem is narrowed to saving, reconstruction, local storage, or export.

steps.title: 3. Verify Study and Patient Context
steps.instructions: Confirm that the correct patient and study are active and that the acquisition completed normally. Check whether the problem affects one study or all newly acquired studies. Expected outcome: An isolated record problem is distinguished from a system-wide processing failure.

steps.title: 4. Check Workstation Responsiveness
steps.instructions: Verify that the acquisition or review workstation is responsive and that no related application is frozen. Check accessible indicators for abnormal workstation behavior. Expected outcome: The processing workstation is functioning normally or a workstation problem is identified.

steps.title: 5. Check Visible Storage Status
steps.instructions: Review normal user-accessible indicators for storage availability, queue status, or pending processing. Do not delete clinical data merely to create space unless following an approved data-management procedure. Expected outcome: No obvious user-visible storage condition is blocking study processing.

steps.title: 6. Inspect External Network Connections
steps.instructions: If the failure involves export or remote storage, check accessible network cables, link status, and connection to the hospital network. Expected outcome: The physical network path is intact.

steps.title: 7. Verify Destination Availability
steps.instructions: Confirm that the intended PACS, oncology information system, archive, or other destination is available. Determine whether other systems are successfully sending to the same destination. Expected outcome: The destination is available or an external server/interface outage is identified.

steps.title: 8. Retry the Appropriate Operation
steps.instructions: After correcting any external workstation, network, or destination issue, retry the save, reconstruction, or export using the existing study when appropriate. Avoid repeating the patient acquisition unless clinically necessary and authorized. Expected outcome: The existing study processes successfully without requiring unnecessary reacquisition.

steps.title: 9. Confirm Data Integrity
steps.instructions: Verify that the completed reconstruction appears correct and that exported data arrives at the intended destination under the correct patient and study. Expected outcome: The full study-processing path is successful. Troubleshooting can stop once integrity and receipt are confirmed.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Processing Failure
steps.instructions: If studies continue to fail after workstation, visible storage, network, and destination checks, stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The affected workflow is removed from clinical use and referred for qualified service or IT evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Radiation Oncology reported that a Versa HD imaging study completed acquisition but would not export to the configured destination.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the affected workstation had lost its external network connection.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering restored the network connection, exported the existing study successfully, and verified correct receipt at the destination before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether save, reconstruction, or export failed

title: Elekta Versa HD Radiation Therapy System - System Will Not Power On or Complete Startup
description: Versa HD does not power on, remains partially initialized, or cannot complete startup because of external power, interlock, peripheral, or communication conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Stop Clinical Use
steps.instructions: Do not continue treatment or troubleshoot the system while a patient depends on it. If a patient is positioned for treatment, follow departmental procedures to safely remove the patient from the treatment position and maintain continuity of care. Check for smoke, unusual odor, excessive heat, fluid intrusion, visible damage, or other immediate hazards. Expected outcome: The patient is safe, the equipment is not being used clinically, and no immediate electrical or mechanical hazard is present. If a hazard exists, remove the system from service and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Startup Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the system is completely without power or whether only part of the Versa HD environment has failed to start. Note which consoles, displays, workstations, gantry indicators, treatment controls, or peripheral devices are powered. Record any displayed messages or abnormal startup behavior exactly as observed. Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to total loss of power, partial startup, or a specific subsystem that is not becoming ready.

steps.title: 3. Verify Facility Power
steps.instructions: Verify that applicable room power, disconnects, breakers, emergency power arrangements, and accessible power connections appear normal. Check whether other equipment supplied from the same electrical area is operating normally. Do not reset facility electrical protection repeatedly if it trips again. Expected outcome: Required facility power is available and stable. If an upstream electrical problem is identified, correct or escalate that condition before troubleshooting the Versa HD further.

steps.title: 4. Check Accessible Power and Emergency Controls
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible power switches, emergency-off controls, and system enable controls for their normal operating state. Verify that an emergency-stop or room emergency control has not been activated. Do not bypass or defeat any safety circuit. Expected outcome: Accessible power and emergency controls are in their intended operating state. If restoring a legitimately activated external control permits normal startup, verify full system operation before stopping troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Inspect External Connections and Peripherals
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible workstation power cords, network connections, peripheral cables, monitors, keyboards, control interfaces, and other external connections for looseness or obvious damage. Reseat only connections intended for routine external service access and only when the system is safely powered down where required. Expected outcome: External connections are secure and undamaged. A loose external connection that restores normal startup identifies a correctable external cause.

steps.title: 6. Verify Room and Infrastructure Conditions
steps.instructions: Check for recent utility interruptions, electrical work, network outages, HVAC problems, equipment relocation, or other room infrastructure events that could affect startup. Verify that room temperature and ventilation appear normal and that equipment ventilation openings are unobstructed. Expected outcome: No unresolved environmental or infrastructure condition is preventing initialization.

steps.title: 7. Perform an Approved Restart if Appropriate
steps.instructions: If no hazard is present and site procedures permit, perform a normal system shutdown and restart using the approved operating sequence. Do not repeatedly cycle power in an attempt to clear a persistent fault. Observe which component fails to initialize. Expected outcome: The Versa HD completes its normal startup sequence. If it does, continue with required functional and safety verification before clinical use.

steps.title: 8. Verify System Readiness
steps.instructions: After successful startup, confirm that operator workstations, treatment controls, positioning systems, imaging components, communication paths, and safety indicators reach their normal ready state. Do not return the system to clinical service based solely on the fact that it powers on. Expected outcome: All required system functions initialize normally and no unresolved fault remains. Troubleshooting can stop after required return-to-service verification is completed.

steps.title: 9. Escalate an Unresolved Startup Failure
steps.instructions: If the system remains unable to complete startup after external power, controls, connections, infrastructure, and approved restart checks are completed, stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The system is removed from clinical service and referred for qualified service evaluation rather than subjected to deeper unauthorized troubleshooting.

CCR.Complaint: Radiation Oncology reported that the Elekta Versa HD powered partially but would not complete startup or enter a treatment-ready state.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an external workstation connection was loose, preventing the affected system component from initializing correctly.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the connection, completed an approved restart, verified normal system initialization, and confirmed required functions before return to service.

title: Elekta Versa HD Radiation Therapy System - Workstation Freezes or Loses Communication
description: A Versa HD workstation freezes, becomes unresponsive, or loses communication because of power, cables, network connectivity, peripheral, software, or infrastructure conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Treatment Workflow
steps.instructions: Do not continue treatment when the workstation or communication path required for safe treatment delivery is frozen or unreliable. Follow departmental procedures to place the patient and equipment in a safe state. Expected outcome: No clinical treatment depends on an unreliable workstation or communication link.

steps.title: 2. Identify the Affected Workstation or Link
steps.instructions: Determine which workstation is affected and whether the problem is a frozen user interface, loss of communication with the treatment system, network disconnection, or failure of a connected peripheral. Record displayed messages and the last successful action. Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to a workstation, network path, peripheral, or wider system issue.

steps.title: 3. Check Basic Power and Indicators
steps.instructions: Verify that the workstation, monitors, network devices accessible to Clinical Engineering, and required peripherals have power. Inspect for abnormal power indicators or unexpected shutdowns. Expected outcome: All required external components are powered normally.

steps.title: 4. Check Keyboard, Mouse, and Display Operation
steps.instructions: Confirm that the issue is not limited to a failed input device or display. Use a known-good compatible peripheral if approved and readily available. Expected outcome: A peripheral problem is distinguished from an actual workstation freeze.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Network and Data Connections
steps.instructions: Check accessible network and system communication cables for loose connectors, damage, disconnected patch cords, or disturbed cable routing. Verify link indicators where they are normally visible. Expected outcome: External communication connections are intact.

steps.title: 6. Determine Whether the Problem Is Local or Widespread
steps.instructions: Check whether other Versa HD workstations or connected systems can communicate normally. If multiple systems are affected, investigate infrastructure availability before assuming a local workstation problem. Expected outcome: The fault is localized to one workstation or identified as an infrastructure-level event.

steps.title: 7. Check for Recent Infrastructure Changes
steps.instructions: Determine whether network maintenance, switch work, power interruption, software deployment, or other system changes occurred near the time of failure. Expected outcome: Any external change potentially related to the outage is identified and routed to the appropriate support group.

steps.title: 8. Perform an Approved Restart
steps.instructions: If the patient is safe and site procedures permit, perform a normal restart of the affected workstation or software environment. Do not repeatedly hard-cycle power or restart active treatment-system components without an approved process. Expected outcome: The workstation restarts, reconnects, and remains responsive.

steps.title: 9. Verify Communication and Workflow
steps.instructions: Confirm that the workstation communicates with required treatment, imaging, record, or network systems and that the affected workflow can be completed using an appropriate nonclinical verification. Expected outcome: Communication remains stable and the required functions work normally. Troubleshooting can stop after applicable verification.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Communication Failure
steps.instructions: If the workstation continues to freeze or lose communication after power, peripherals, network connections, infrastructure, and approved restart checks, stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The affected system is withheld from clinical use until service-level evaluation is completed.

CCR.Complaint: Radiation Oncology reported that a Versa HD workstation became unresponsive and stopped communicating with the treatment system.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a loose external network connection at the affected workstation.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the connection, restarted the workstation using the approved process, and verified stable communication and normal workflow before return to service.
